10:1.sourceText: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα ἀνέδειξεν ὁ Κύριος ἑτέρους ἑβδομήκοντα, καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς ἀνὰ δύο πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ εἰς πᾶσαν πόλιν καὶ τόπον οὗ ἤμελλεν αὐτὸς ἔρχεσθαι.
10:1.targetText: After this, the Lord appointed seventy-two others and sent them two by two ahead of Him to every town and place He was about to visit.

groups.note: ἀνὰ δύο ("two apiece") is rendered two by two.
πρὸ προσώπου ("before the face of") is rendered ahead of.

διακονίαν ("serving") is rendered the preparations to be made.
μέλει σοι ("is it a concern to you") is rendered do You care.
Same verb, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering δέ.
BSB leaves οὖν ("so") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the person; the participle ἐπιστᾶσα has no object.
English joins the participle ἐπιστᾶσα and the main verb with and.

10:41.sourceText: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ ὁ Κύριος Μάρθα Μάρθα, μεριμνᾷς καὶ θορυβάζῃ περὶ πολλά,
10:41.targetText: “Martha, Martha,” the Lord replied, “you are worried and upset about many things.

groups.note: ἀποκριθεὶς … εἶπεν ("answering, said") is rendered by one verb.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
BSB leaves αὐτῇ ("to her") unexpressed.

10:42.sourceText: ὀλίγων δέ ἐστιν χρεία ἢ ἑνός· Μαριὰμ γὰρ τὴν ἀγαθὴν μερίδα ἐξελέξατο, ἥτις οὐκ ἀφαιρεθήσεται αὐτῆς.
10:42.targetText: But only one thing is necessary. Mary has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her.”

groups.note: The relative ἥτις ("which") is rendered and it.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render ὀλίγων … ἤ ("few things, or"); its wording keeps only the alternative "one".
BSB leaves γάρ ("for") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English stresses that one thing alone is needed.
